decisions.reason: The flagship citrus harvesting crate serves a specialized agricultural niche where reusable crates are gaining adoption, and keeping a tooled injection-molded product costs little while its value is still unfolding.
Foldable large containers are a core and growing category in returnable packaging, and its sustained own-page presentation signals ongoing commitment rather than a fading option.
A stackable crate is a low-cost staple of the range, already amortized in tooling and cheap to keep, so abandoning it releases few resources.
Rackable pallets serve steady industrial and retail demand at low holding cost, so the option is worth keeping open.

Its shift from its own page to a mere mention suggests less emphasis, but the niche spill-retention pallet remains cheap to keep within a broad portfolio and does not yet show clear evidence of failure.
The pallet with load retainers was also demoted to a mention, hinting at weaker prospects, yet its low maintenance cost argues for keeping it rather than dropping it.
